parsed.explanation: The combined regime creates several traveller-facing exposures: national entry screening can refuse or flag sex-marker/document discrepancies and raise lifetime fraud ineligibility; immigration custody and state prison placement by birth sex carry documented abuse; the division's executive order backs sex-segregated facilities; under-19 care is banned. National hate-crime coverage, marriage recognition, legal-aid guidance and court injunctions are partial climate/protection signals, but they do not offset border, facility or custody exposure. A short-stay adult may avoid some state institutions, but outing at the border or any detention escalates severity sharply. Minors travelling with guardians face the care ban and heightened document scrutiny. Score reflects high severity conditional on outing/detention, not routine street targeting.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules bar self-selected markers on passports/visas, stop new X markers, and instruct officers to refuse cases with sex/document doubts; suspected misrepresentation can yield lifetime immigration fraud ineligibility. Advisories and detentions of neighbouring citizens are documented.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry for some holders; litigation challenges the passport policy; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Foreign visitors use home passports, but border officers apply national screening; a mismatch can trigger secondary inspection, refusal, or detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse against trans men; national prisons adopted conversion-style policies. Division prison places by birth sex; a trans woman was celled with a male sex offender and her failure-to-protect claim was dismissed.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; some national orders enjoined; no division custody protection documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border refusal can lead to immigration detention; any local arrest can lead to birth-sex custody. Protections do not reach placement or abuse.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division executive order defines sex at birth and backs single-sex bathrooms/changing rooms in state settings; national map shows facility bans in many divisions. No criminal bathroom ban is recorded in this division, but government facilities may exclude.
federal_state_facilities.protection: No visitor-facing facility protection documented; local anti-discrimination ordinances do not clearly cover facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State EO and national definitions reinforce each other; private venues may be less covered, government buildings and custody are the sharp edge.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for anyone under 19 is banned and upheld; a visitor cannot obtain it for a minor in their care. Adult care is not documented as banned.
care_services.protection: No protection for minors; national litigation on related rules is unresolved.
care_services.interaction: Adult traveller may access routine care, but a guardian of a trans minor faces the ban; emergency discovery can expose identity.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups among priorities; DOJ reward guidance uses 'radical gender ideology'; division EO directs agencies to biological-sex definitions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute; courts have blocked some orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing raises police/border suspicion and can worsen treatment if stopped; protection is national and uneven locally.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minors face under-19 care ban, school-transition prosecution directives, athletics bans and document scrutiny; a guardian travelling with a trans minor may face questioning.
minors_guardians.protection: No division protection; national injunctions partial.
minors_guardians.interaction: Border document mismatch plus state care/school rules compound risk for families.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division trans violence statistics are sourced; national advisories warn trans travellers; division hate-crime law omits gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; local ordinances vary.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A victim may get national charge but no state hate-crime enhancement; police response to trans visitors is not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Division has no statewide gender-identity anti-discrimination law; marker rules for locally issued IDs are unresolved after EO; care ban upheld.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National employment/housing protections, marriage recognition, legal-aid guidance, and court challenges exist.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: National remedies may operate for some harms but do not remedy border refusal, facility exclusion or custody placement; litigation leaves operative rules uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in that a trans person can be arrested/humiliated and held in hostile custody; this dossier lacks documented street extortion but adds national border refusal/lifetime-ban risk and state prison assault dismissal. Conditional custody severity is higher, but arbitrary arrest is less documented, so rating slightly above 0.25-C.

Anchor ends at invasive administrative review and denial of entry without detention. This dossier shares entry refusal but adds immigration/state custody abuse and facility exclusion, so it sits below 0.35-A.
Anchor has temporary delay and eventual permit with no custody. This dossier has refusal/lifetime ineligibility, facility exclusion, and documented custody harm, so materially lower.
Anchor shows protection operating after friction. Here remedies are partial and do not reach border, facilities or custody; much lower.

parsed.synthesis: National entry screening is the first and most universal gate: a trans visitor with a marker/appearance discrepancy can be refused, stranded, or face lifetime fraud ineligibility; if detained, immigration custody has documented abuse. The division adds a hostile second layer—sex-at-birth definitions, single-sex facilities, under-19 care ban, and birth-sex prison placement with a dismissed assault claim. National hate-crime coverage, marriage recognition, legal-aid guidance and court injunctions are real but partial; they do not cancel the border, facility or custody exposures. An adult short-stay traveller may avoid local institutions, but outing at the border or any arrest escalates severity sharply; a guardian with a trans minor faces the care ban and document scrutiny.
